Algoma WI (port locode USAGM) is a Lake Michigan cruise port and town in Wisconsin USA (Kewaunee County) with population around 3,000. Algoma is at the Ahnapee River's mouth and is road-connected with Sturgeon Bay (via highway WIS 42) to the north and with Kewaunee to the south, as well as with Green Bay (via highway WIS 54) to the west.

Watercraft (boats, yachts and cruise ships) dock at Hill Pier 42 Marina.

Being one of the Great Lakes, Lake Michigan has surface area (22300 mi2/58000 km2), water volume (1180 mi3/4900 km3) max depth (925 ft/282 m), cities in Illinois (Chicago), Indiana (Gary), Wisconsin (Green Bay, Sheboygan, Milwaukee, Kenosha, Racine) and Michigan (Muskegon, Traverse City).

Currently, the largest by capacity Great Lakes cruise companies are Viking Cruises USA (ships Viking Octantis, Viking Polaris), AQV-American Queen Voyages (ships Ocean Navigator, Ocean Voyager), Pearl Seas Cruises (Pearl Mist), and the Canadian company St Lawrence Cruise Lines (Canadian Empress). Other travel brands that offer Great Lakes voyages are PONANT and Tauck (fleet).

Algoma WI's most popular tourist activities include sports fishing, sailing, leisure boating, trailing, Since 2000, the town holds annually the Algoma Car Show (in June, showcasing classical cars and trucks), Shanty Days Fair (in August, presenting foods, draft beer, wine tasting, live music, arts and crafts show, fireworks, parade) and The Park Concerts Series (in July-August).

The settlement was established in the mid-19th-century (1834). The town (as Wolf River) was founded in 1851, renamed Ahnapee in 1859, incorporated in 1879, and renamed Algoma in 1897. One of the town's major industries was commercial fishing, having the largest fishing fleet on Lake Michigan.

Algoma started to develop following the integration into A&W (Ahnapee and Western Railway, length 35 mi / 56 km) which interconnected Sturgeon Bay (northern terminus), Maplewood, Forestville, Algoma, Casco, Kewaunee, Green Bay (southern/western terminus). Part of the historic A&W railroad is the current-day Ahnapee State Trail - a multi-purpose trail for activities like hiking, biking, horse riding, and snowmobiling. The trail runs the former Green Bay and Western Railroad's line from Casco Junction to Sturgeon Bay.

At a Glance

Independent with some planning. Algoma is a compact, walkable Lake Michigan town. Once ashore, passengers can independently explore Crescent Beach, the waterfront and downtown without needing a vehicle. Longer trips into Door County are better suited to an organized excursion.

  • Arrival: Large cruise ships normally anchor offshore and ferry passengers ashore by tender.
  • Main sights: Crescent Beach and Boardwalk, downtown murals, the Ahnapee River waterfront and local shops and galleries.
  • Terrain: Generally flat and easy, although the beach itself has sand.
  • Suggested local visit: Approximately 2–4 hours.

Getting from the Cruise Ship

Cruise ships normally remain offshore because the harbor cannot accommodate large expedition vessels. Tenders bring passengers into the Algoma marina area near Heritage Park and downtown. The exact landing point and passenger arrangements can vary by call.

Most local attractions are within a short walk of the waterfront, so taxis are unnecessary for exploring Algoma itself. Tender operations may be slowed or changed by Lake Michigan conditions; allow extra time for the return trip and follow the ship’s stated last-tender time.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Crescent Beach and Boardwalk

This is Algoma’s easiest independent outing. The public lakefront park includes a sandy beach, grassy areas, benches and an accessible boardwalk approximately 0.8 km (0.5 mi) long. Allow 45–90 minutes for a relaxed shoreline walk, photography or beachcombing. Lake Michigan water can remain cold even in summer, and conditions may be windy.

Downtown Murals, Shops and Galleries

Algoma’s compact center contains outdoor historical murals, small galleries, independent shops and places for refreshments. A self-guided mural brochure may be available from the Algoma Visitor Center. Allow approximately 1–2 hours; this is easy to combine with the beach and waterfront.

Ahnapee River Waterfront and Local Tasting

Walk along the harbor and lower Ahnapee River, then visit downtown businesses or the historic von Stiehl Winery. Tastings and tours depend on the day’s operating schedule, so confirm availability before relying on them. This option is practical independently and usually requires 1–2 hours.

Ahnapee State Trail

The Ahnapee State Trail provides a mostly level, firm-surface route through the river corridor and surrounding countryside. Cruise visitors should treat it as an out-and-back walk rather than attempt a distant destination. A short section of 3–6 km (1.9–3.7 mi) can fit into a port call, with approximately 1–2 hours required.

Door County

Algoma can serve as a gateway to the Door Peninsula. Sturgeon Bay is roughly a 20–30-minute drive away, while Peninsula State Park and the bay-side villages require considerably more travel. A broad Door County highlights trip commonly occupies about five hours or longer.

There is no practical public transport for a flexible sightseeing circuit from the tender landing. An organized excursion is recommended because it coordinates transportation and return timing. Passengers on shorter calls should remain in Algoma rather than attempt the northern peninsula independently.

Self-Guided Waterfront and Downtown Walk

Difficulty: Easy, mostly flat
Distance: Approximately 3 km (1.9 mi)
Pure walking time: About 40–50 minutes
Recommended time with stops: 2–3 hours

  1. Tender landing and Heritage Park: Begin near the marina and take in views across the harbor and Ahnapee River mouth.
  2. Downtown Algoma: Walk inland toward Steele Street, looking for the large historical murals on downtown buildings.
  3. Lower Ahnapee River: Continue through the compact commercial area and along the riverfront.
  4. Visitor Center: Stop for a local map and current information before reaching the lakefront.
  5. Crescent Beach Boardwalk: Follow the boardwalk beside Lake Michigan, using the benches and beach access points as desired.
  6. Marina return: Walk back along the waterfront toward the tender landing.

The route can be shortened by turning back at any point along the boardwalk. The boardwalk is accessible, but beach access involves sand.

Lighthouse and Pier Notice

The Algoma Pierhead Lighthouse is normally a prominent waterfront landmark. However, a multi-year North Pier rehabilitation project began in 2026, and the lighthouse was temporarily removed for restoration. Pier access may be closed or restricted during construction. View the harbor only from open public areas and obey all barriers.

Practical Tips

  • Wear layers because the lakeshore can be substantially cooler and windier than inland areas.
  • Check the ship’s tender schedule before starting any walk; the last tender may depart well before the published sailing time.
  • Local museums, galleries, tours and tasting rooms may have seasonal or limited opening hours.
  • Arrange transport in advance for any independent trip beyond Algoma; taxis and rideshare vehicles may be limited.
  • Allow a generous return margin for traffic, tender queues and changing lake conditions.
